book.title: Career and Technical Education Grade 7 Student Textbook
book.subject: cte
book.unit_title: Introduction to Career and Technical Education (CTE)

title: Unit summary and review questions
competency: Bring together the ideas of Unit 1.

keywords.def: The path of progress a person follows to reach their life goals.
Legal work that gives a service or goods and earns money.
Teaching skills-based careers to students. Short form: CTE.

en.text: A career is a lifelong process of growth, like climbing a ladder. A job is what you do now for income. CTE gives hands-on experience, opens jobs and is a base for further education.

screens.title: Unit summary
paras: A career aims to improve your skills so you can grow or move to another job.
Getting a job is a one-time event. A career is a lifelong process, like climbing a ladder.
Think about the work you want and the education you need.
CTE gives hands-on experience and prepares you for technical careers.
CTE offers jobs, reduces unemployment and is a base for further education.

screens.title: Key words of the unit
defs: A lifelong path of growth toward your goals.
Legal work that earns money now.
Education that joins learning with practical work skills.

pairs: What you do now for income
screens.clue: Start with the one you are sure of.

screens.why: Getting a job is a one-time event; a career is lifelong.
screens.clue: Which one is like a ladder?

screens.text: To plan a career, you should think about:
opts: The work you want and the education you need
screens.ans: The work you want and the education you need

screens.text: Abebe says: "I will take any job today and never learn anything new." What does he miss about careers?
opts: A career means growing skills over time
screens.ans: A career means growing skills over time
screens.why: A career has a goal of improving your skills so you can grow in your job or move into another one.
screens.clue: What does a career aim to improve?

items.why: A career is a lifelong process.

items.text: Career and job are not related.
CTE does not involve acquiring knowledge.
items.why: CTE combines knowledge with technical skills.

items.text: Career is for immediate gain but job is future oriented.
CTE focuses more on academic learning.
items.clue: What does the T stand for?

items.ask: ___ is future-oriented and job is short-term.
items.why: A career looks to future growth.
items.clue: The opposite of a short-term job.

items.ask: What one wants to be in the future is ___.
items.why: An aspiration (life goal); the path to it is a career.

items.ask: ___ links school learning with the world of work.
items.why: CTE connects classroom learning and work.

items.text: Which sentence best describes the relationship and difference of job and career?
opts: They are related: a career is made of one or more jobs, but a job is work now while a career is lifelong growth
They have nothing to do with each other
items.ans: They are related: a career is made of one or more jobs, but a job is work now while a career is lifelong growth
items.why: A career can be one job or a series of jobs through advancement. A job is what you do now for income.

notes.text: The chapter test draws 20 questions round-robin from the four section tests (5 each), no clues, 25 minutes.
Review II Q2: the book's wording fits "aspiration" as well as "career"; both are accepted.
Review I Q5: the book does not say directly which CTE focuses on more; "False" follows from its stress on technical, hands-on skills.
Review III Q1 asks for a written answer; it is turned into a multiple choice with the book-based model answer.
